package bookstore

import "sort"

// Cost returns the minimum total price, in cents, for the given basket of books.
// Each book is identified by an integer 1-5.
func Cost(books []int) int {
	var counts [5]int
	for _, b := range books {
		if b >= 1 && b <= 5 {
			counts[b-1]++
		}
	}
	return minCost(counts[:])
}

// groupPrice is the price of a group of k distinct books, in cents.
var groupPrice = [6]int{0, 800, 1520, 2160, 2560, 3000}

func minCost(counts []int) int {
	// memo keyed by the count vector
	memo := map[[5]int]int{}
	var solve func(c [5]int) int
	solve = func(c [5]int) int {
		if c == ([5]int{}) {
			return 0
		}
		if v, ok := memo[c]; ok {
			return v
		}
		best := -1
		// try every non-empty subset of titles with copies remaining
		for mask := 1; mask < 32; mask++ {
			k := 0
			next := c
			ok := true
			for t := 0; t < 5; t++ {
				if mask&(1<<t) != 0 {
					if c[t] == 0 {
						ok = false
						break
					}
					next[t]--
					k++
				}
			}
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			cost := groupPrice[k] + solve(next)
			if best < 0 || cost < best {
				best = cost
			}
		}
		memo[c] = best
		return best
	}
	return solve(counts)
}

func minCost(counts [5]int) int {
	memo := make(map[[5]int]int)
	var solve func(c [5]int) int
	solve = func(c [5]int) int {
		if c == ([5]int{}) {
			return 0
		}
		if v, ok := memo[c]; ok {
			return v
		}
		best := 0
		for mask := 1; mask < 1<<5; mask++ {
			size := 0
			next := c
			valid := true
			for t := 0; t < 5; t++ {
				if mask&(1<<t) != 0 {
					if c[t] == 0 {
						valid = false
						break
					}
					next[t]--
					size++
				}
			}
			if !valid {
				continue
			}
			cost := groupPrice[size] + solve(next)
			if best == 0 || cost < best {
				best = cost
			}
		}
		memo[c] = best
		return best
	}
	return solve(counts)
}

1. **`Cost(books []int) int`** counts copies per title (1–5) and hands off to the optimizer.
2. **`minCost`** is a memoized search over the per-title count vector: at each step it tries every possible next group — one copy of each title in any non-empty subset — paying the group's discounted price, and keeps the cheapest total. 3. **`groupPrice`** holds the per-group prices in cents: 800 / 1520 / 2160 / 2560 / 3000 for groups of 1–5 (the 0%/5%/10%/20%/25% discounts on $8 books).
